seo.title: TablePro vs Postico: PostgreSQL tools and licensing
seo.description: Postico 2 is a Mac app for PostgreSQL with one-time licenses. TablePro covers PostgreSQL and other engines. Compare prices, server tools, sync and setup.

header.title: TablePro vs Postico
header.lead: Postico focuses on PostgreSQL and databases that speak its protocol. TablePro connects to PostgreSQL and other database types. Compare their query tools, server tools and licenses.

tablepro: Free roles, sessions, VACUUM and pg_dump tools.
competitor: A focused client for PostgreSQL-compatible databases, including Greenplum.
A Mac App Store copy or a one-time license.
Server settings synced through iCloud or Dropbox.

glance.intro: Postico 2 is sold with one-time licenses for personal, commercial, team and student use, and its evaluation version has no time limit. TablePro is free to use, and its paid plans add optional features.

administration.label: Server administration
administration.tablepro: Free in the Mac app: Users & Roles, a Server Dashboard, maintenance such as VACUUM, and backups through pg_dump, which you install

macAppStore.label: Mac App Store
macAppStore.tablepro: Not on the Mac App Store. Download it from this site or install it with Homebrew

items.text: Postico 2 is built for PostgreSQL and the databases that speak its protocol, including Greenplum, which TablePro does not support.
A license is paid once, with prices for personal, commercial, team and student use, and there is a copy on the Mac App Store.
The evaluation version has no time limit, though some features stay off until you buy a license.
Server settings sync through iCloud or Dropbox.
One client covers PostgreSQL and other engines, from MySQL and SQL Server to Redis, MongoDB and DuckDB. See the <link>supported databases</link>.

<link>Server work</link> is in the free app: Users & Roles with grants down to a column, a Server Dashboard with sessions and slow queries, and VACUUM with the SQL shown first. Postico says it is not designed for these tasks.
<link>EXPLAIN</link> shows a plan as a diagram, a tree or raw text, and EXPLAIN Compare checks a new plan against a baseline. Both are free.
<link>iCloud Sync</link> syncs connections across Macs, iPhones and iPads. It requires Starter on the Mac and is free on iPhone and iPad.
A free <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> connects to PostgreSQL, with no in-app purchases.
Greenplum is not among the supported engines.
Redshift and CockroachDB connect, but their table structure is read-only in TablePro.
To change a PostgreSQL column’s position, TablePro writes a rebuild script for you to run. It does not run the script itself.

Postico 2 is sold only as one-time licenses. TablePro offers subscriptions and one-time purchases. Subscriptions lock paid features when they end; the free app keeps working. One-time purchases do not expire.

switching.intro: TablePro has no importer for Postico. Add each server as a TablePro connection: fill in the connection form, or paste a URL that starts with postgresql:// into <ui>File > Import > Import from URL…</ui>
after: If a project keeps its database URL in a .env file or a Prisma schema, <ui>File > Import > Open Project Folder…</ui> reads it and opens the connection form filled in.
Passwords go into the macOS Keychain. TablePro also reads ~/.pgpass for PostgreSQL connections.
Query history starts fresh in TablePro.

faq.question: Does TablePro work with Redshift and CockroachDB like Postico?
faq.answer: Yes, both connect, and their table structure is read-only in TablePro. Greenplum, which Postico also supports, is not among TablePro’s engines.

faq.question: Is TablePro’s iCloud Sync free?
faq.answer: In the iPhone and iPad app, yes. On the Mac it is part of Starter. Postico 2 syncs server settings through iCloud or Dropbox.

faq.question: Can I manage roles and sessions in TablePro?
faq.answer: Yes, in the Mac app and for free. Users & Roles grants and revokes privileges with the SQL shown first, and the Server Dashboard lists sessions and can terminate one. <link>Read about server tools</link>.

notes.postico-evaluation: Evaluation version with no time limit. Some features are disabled until you buy a license.
notes.postico-databases: PostgreSQL, Amazon Redshift, Greenplum and CockroachDB. Other databases that speak the PostgreSQL protocol may connect, but most features will not work.
notes.postico-sync-icloud-dropbox: Server settings sync through iCloud or Dropbox
notes.postico-no-admin: Postico says it is not designed for backup and restore, user and permission management, or database monitoring
